title: BEN Group Securities Trading Policy (version 4.0)

tiers.name: BEN Personnel
tiers.description: All directors, executives, employees, contractors and consultants of BEN Group. Subject only to the fundamental insider trading prohibitions in section 1.1; the section 1.2 restrictions (clearance, 30-day holding, speculative trading, short selling, margin loans, hedging) apply only to Designated Officers.

tiers.name: Designated Officers
tiers.description: BEN Personnel most likely to possess inside information, in three categories: Tier 1 - Board and Executive Leadership (all Directors of BEN Group, and the CEO & Managing Director); Tier 2 - Senior Management (Executive Committee members, Divisional Executive Managers, Senior Leadership Group members, Company Secretary); Tier 3 - Key Personnel (all personnel in Corporate Secretariat, Corporate Development, Group Strategy, Investor Relations, Corporate Affairs, Public Relations, Group Legal, Group Internal Audit, Treasury & Tax, Financial Control, Financial Planning & Analysis, STL Management & STL Investments, Reward Performance & Governance and Marketing Operations, plus Executive Assistants, people leaders in Finance and in Group Risk, and anyone else designated by the Board). All section 1.2 restrictions apply uniformly across the three tiers, which differ only in the approving officer.

tiers.name: Board Chair
tiers.description: Tier 1 Designated Officer; clearance to trade is approved by the Chair of the People & Culture Committee. The Board Chair also approves 'other exceptional circumstances' exemptions under section 7.1.

tiers.name: Other Directors (including CEO)
tiers.description: Tier 1 Designated Officers other than the Board Chair, including the CEO & Managing Director; clearance approved by the Board Chair.

tiers.name: Executive Committee members
tiers.description: Tier 2 Designated Officers; clearance approved by the CEO.

tiers.name: All other Designated Officers and close connections
tiers.description: Residual Tier 2 and Tier 3 Designated Officers and the close connections of any Designated Officer; clearance approved by the Company Secretary.

tiers.name: Close Connections
tiers.description: Family members (parents, spouse or partner and dependent children), entities controlled by the Designated Officer or their family, and trusts where the Designated Officer or family are beneficiaries. They are subject to the same restrictions and clearance requirements, and the Designated Officer must take all reasonable steps to ensure they comply.

definitions.hedging_definition: Enter into hedging transactions to limit the economic risk of their holdings in BEN securities. This applies to both unvested and vested entitlements.

windows.end_anchor: the start of the trading day after half-year results are released to the ASX
the start of the trading day after full-year results are released to the ASX

windows.end_anchor: approximately 30 days after the results announcement

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board determines ad hoc Blackout Periods, imposed when considering material announcements, applying to specific individuals or to all Designated Officers. The Company Secretary provides notification of Blackout Periods to BEN personnel. The Policy does not state that ad hoc blackouts are confidential, but a refusal of clearance must be kept confidential. The Board may also determine additional Trading Windows.

rules.detail: BEN Securities include 'any derivatives relating to BEN Group securities', with no venue limitation, and Trading is 'any action taken to buy, sell, transfer, or otherwise deal in securities'. A purchased put and written call over a BEN holding are hedging transactions limiting economic risk and are therefore prohibited outright for Designated Officers, whether the underlying entitlements are vested or unvested; a derivative that was not a hedge would still require prior written clearance and could not be short-term or speculative.
rules.evidence: Enter into hedging transactions to limit the economic risk of their holdings in BEN securities. This applies to both unvested and vested entitlements.

rules.detail: The section 1.2 additional restrictions, including the hedging ban, apply only to Designated Officers. Other BEN Personnel are subject only to the insider trading prohibitions.

Flat prohibition on hedging transactions limiting the economic risk of BEN holdings, expressly extended to vested entitlements. No clearance route: hedging is listed as a thing Designated Officers 'must not' do, not as a dealing requiring clearance, and the section 7 exemptions cover only trading during blackout periods in exceptional circumstances.
rules.evidence: Designated Officers must not: ... Enter into hedging transactions to limit the economic risk of their holdings in BEN securities. This applies to both unvested and vested entitlements.

rules.detail: The same prohibition is expressly stated to apply to unvested entitlements, so performance rights and unvested share awards cannot be hedged.
rules.evidence: This applies to both unvested and vested entitlements.

rules.detail: Close connections are subject to the restrictions on Designated Officers, and the Designated Officer must take all reasonable steps to ensure they comply, so the hedging ban cannot be avoided by routing the structure through a family trust or controlled entity.
rules.evidence: The following close connections of Designated Officers are also subject to restrictions: Family members ... Entities controlled by the Designated Officer or their family. Trusts where the Designated Officer or family are beneficiaries.

rules.detail: The hedging ban is confined to Designated Officers; BEN Personnel generally are not addressed.

Monetisation structures are not named, but a prepaid forward, collar or exchangeable limits the economic risk of a BEN holding and so falls within the hedging prohibition; if it involves borrowing against the shares it is also caught by the ban on using BEN securities as security for margin loans or similar financing arrangements.
rules.evidence: Enter into hedging transactions to limit the economic risk of their holdings in BEN securities.

rules.detail: Outright ban on short selling BEN securities, with no qualification for covered positions and no clearance route.
rules.evidence: Designated Officers must not: ... Short sell BEN securities.

rules.detail: Securities lending is not named. It would involve a transfer, which is Trading, and so would require clearance for a Designated Officer, but the Policy is otherwise silent.

CFDs are not named, but a CFD over BEN securities is a derivative relating to BEN Group securities and either hedges the holder's economic risk or amounts to speculative or short-term trading, both of which are prohibited for Designated Officers.
rules.evidence: Engage in speculative or short-term trading in BEN securities for short-term gains.

rules.detail: Designated Officers must not use BEN securities as security for margin loans. 'Margin loans' is defined broadly in the glossary as 'a loan that allows borrowers to borrow money for investment purposes'. There is no approval or exemption route.
rules.evidence: Use BEN securities as security for entering into margin loans or similar financing arrangements.

rules.detail: Using BEN securities as security is prohibited where it is for a margin loan or similar financing arrangement. A charge or pledge unconnected with any financing is not named, although a transfer of the securities to a security trustee or nominee would itself be Trading requiring clearance.
rules.evidence: Use BEN securities as security for entering into margin loans or similar financing arrangements.

rules.detail: The prohibition is not confined to margin loans: it extends to 'similar financing arrangements' secured on BEN securities, which covers a bank facility secured on a collared parcel. It applies to all Designated Officers and their close connections, to vested and unvested holdings alike, and has no clearance, hardship or Board waiver route.
rules.evidence: Use BEN securities as security for entering into margin loans or similar financing arrangements.

rules.detail: The financing restriction sits in section 1.2 and applies only to Designated Officers.

Two limbs: a mechanical minimum holding period of 30 days, and a broader ban on speculative or short-term trading for short-term gains. Vesting of performance rights and share awards and the exercise of options are carved out of the clearance regime by section 8.2, but subsequent trading activity is not.
rules.evidence: Designated Officers must not: ... Hold BEN securities for less than 30 days. Engage in speculative or short-term trading in BEN securities for short-term gains.

clearance.evidence: All Designated Officers and close connections must obtain written clearance from the approving officer before trading BEN securities during Trading Windows

clearance.evidence: Clearance, if approved, is valid for 5 business days unless withdrawn. The decision to grant or refuse clearance is at the Approving Officer's absolute discretion.

clearance.evidence: If clearance is refused, that decision must be kept confidential. Clearances do not reflect an endorsement of the trade.

exemption_authority: Section 7: Designated Officers and close connections may apply in writing to the Company Secretary to trade during blackout periods only in exceptional circumstances - severe financial hardship, court orders or legal requirements, or other exceptional circumstances approved by the Board Chair - demonstrating that disposal is the only reasonable option and that they hold no inside information; exemptions are recorded in the approved exemption register and reported to the relevant Divisional Risk Committee. The exemption power is confined to trading during blackout periods and cannot authorise hedging, short selling or secured financing, which are absolute prohibitions in section 1.2.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Enter into hedging transactions to limit the economic risk of their holdings in BEN securities. This applies to both unvested and vested entitlements.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The derivative legs of a collar are prohibited outright for every Designated Officer over fully vested shares, with no clearance or exemption route, which defeats the structure at the first step.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Use BEN securities as security for entering into margin loans or similar financing arrangements.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The words 'or similar financing arrangements' extend past classic margin lending to any loan secured on BEN securities, so the funding leg is prohibited independently of the hedging ban.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Officers and close connections may apply to trade during blackout periods only in exceptional circumstances
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The only discretionary relief in the Policy is permission to trade during a blackout period; nothing empowers the Board Chair, CEO or Company Secretary to waive the hedging or secured financing prohibitions.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The following close connections of Designated Officers are also subject to restrictions: Family members - Parents, spouse/partner and dependent children. Entities controlled by the Designated Officer or their family. Trusts where the Designated Officer or family are beneficiaries.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar written on shares held by a family trust or controlled entity is caught, and the Designated Officer is obliged to take reasonable steps to ensure the entity complies.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Trading: Any action taken to buy, sell, transfer, or otherwise deal in securities. Transfer: Administrative transfers of securities between own accounts or to personal superannuation funds.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no carve-out for dealings with no change in beneficial interest, so even moving the collateral parcel into a custody or security trustee account is Trading requiring prior written clearance inside a Trading Window.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Hold BEN securities for less than 30 days.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any physically settled leg of a collar must not result in shares being acquired and disposed of within 30 days, which constrains cash-settled substitution and early unwind mechanics.

bespoke_clauses.clause: BEN Securities: Includes shares, options, rights, debentures or any derivatives relating to BEN Group securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Every leg of an OTC collar is itself a BEN Security, so entering, amending or closing it is Trading and is caught by the clearance regime as well as the hedging ban.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Share Registry Provider (MUFG): Monitor controls and provide alerts placed on Designated Officers in the share registry. ... Flagged Holdings Reports when Designated Officers trade.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Registry alerts are placed on Designated Officer holdings, so any transfer of the collateral parcel to a bank nominee would be detected and reported to the Company Secretary.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The decision to grant or refuse clearance is at the Approving Officer's absolute discretion. If clearance is refused, that decision must be kept confidential.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even for permitted trades the executive cannot explain a refusal to the bank, so no timetable dependent on clearance can be contractually guaranteed.

summary: A funded collar is not available to any BEN Designated Officer. Section 1.2 prohibits Designated Officers from entering into hedging transactions to limit the economic risk of their holdings in BEN securities and states expressly that this applies to vested as well as unvested entitlements, so the put and call legs are banned outright with no clearance route; short selling is separately prohibited. The funding leg is independently blocked, because Designated Officers must not use BEN securities as security for margin loans 'or similar financing arrangements', wording that reaches a bank facility secured on the collared parcel. The prohibitions extend to close connections, including family trusts and controlled entities, and the only discretionary relief in the Policy is permission to trade during a blackout period in cases of severe financial hardship or court order, which cannot waive the hedging or financing bans. Even ordinary dealing is tightly controlled: written clearance from the designated approving officer, valid five business days and revocable, trading only in the roughly 30-day window after each results announcement, and a 30-day minimum holding period.
